target.name: PreyVR touch panels and native hacking input integration, supported Steam x64 target

question: Can touch-panel presses and controller hacking use the existing UI/input seams while preserving tracking, modal-content and delivered-input ownership in source and offline fixtures?
claim: The supported Steam bytes and installed base/patch profiles identify DanielleHacking2 and exactly ten hacking actions, covering six Xbox bindings and four keyboard-only directions. The integrated adapter routes left stick and X/Y/A/B through normal native input, preserving native action-map filtering. Offline fixtures confirm bounded flat/cylinder poke crossing, rejection of stale/context/panel-motion discontinuities, ray/touch handoff, menu-content invalidation and bidirectional gameplay/hacking cleanup interlocks. Both optional features are saved, off by default and exposed on the Input options page. This confirms static/source and fixture contracts only.
method: MSVC x64 Release 19.50.35729.0 with Visual Studio 18 2026 and CMake/CTest, Python 3.12 read-only supported-module/PAK verification. Actual native adapters and production options painter run with explicit external input/tracking/HUD substitutions; pure geometry/input state machines also run. Controls include corrupting a native witness, removing or adding an action-map entry, stale/context-changed samples, stationary finger vs moving panel, refused vs acknowledged cleanup, and a first face press closing the modal before a simultaneous second press. Source.patch and REPRODUCE.md retain source changes and commands. The initial harness failure was equal-QPC-timestamp fixture publications; the fixture now waits for a strictly newer real timestamp. Final combined suite passes 80/80. No game launch, process attachment, xr-sim session or headset test.

identity.reason: Full source commit, previous integration base and fetched collaborator tips are frozen. Native verifier requires Steam module SHA256 7D6E322F61B28331095A400F0BA5F09BD9A39C57BF993602285DD6ACB05311A7. Tested DLL, package and archive identities are recorded.

instrument.reason: Native witness and bounded PAK decoder checks include deliberately corrupted-byte and action-map mutations, CRCs and Twofish known-answer validation. Fixtures compile actual adapters with documented boundary substitutions; GDI uses the actual production painter. Package checker matches all local and ZIP manifest files plus the tested DLL.

control.reason: Valid hover/crossing versus behind-entry, stale source, moved/resized surface and changed context; successful versus refused native cleanup; simultaneous faces with modal exit; complete base/patch maps versus missing/extra-action mutations. Previous offline baseline retained in the 80-test combined suite.

scene.reason: Offline synthetic native-boundary/graphics fixtures and static game files, not a running Prey scene.

restore.reason: Persistent version-controlled source edits and a separate new local test package. No game, user VR preferences or shared runtime configuration changed. Launcher DryRun refused because another fleet game was running; it was left alone.

baseline.reason: Final Release build and 80/80 offline tests pass; actual production options raster inspected and package/ZIP hashes match. This is source/harness health. Native/headset acceptance is not measured, and the launcher dry run was blocked by the fleet guard.

limits: No native puzzle input acceptance, pause timing, rendering/framing, inventory drag/drop, physical-controller alignment, comfort or performance measured. Default profiles do not prove custom user remaps. Touch is a selected-controller aim-tip proxy, not optical finger tracking or a new native pointing animation. Brief pokes can be refused if the game misses neutral hover. Internal stereoscopic UI-layer depth and world-behind-inventory rendering are unchanged. A successful native post does not prove the puzzle consumed it. Windows PowerShell 5.1 launcher DryRun refused while SystemShock2Remastered was running; no game was stopped or launched. A local test package is prepared, not a released or headset-approved build.
